subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
subtype: Approach: contingency plan with spare parts [Thinking]
passage: So what's in our repair kit? Two spare batteries, a spare sensor, a roll of wire, a small screwdriver set, tape and a soldering pen. I'm Sabina, and our box has a list taped inside the lid. Seema is our repair person; her only job at the event is to fix things while the rest of us run the robot. In the second round a wire came loose and the robot froze on the line. Seema had it reconnected in four minutes with the tools from the box. Without the kit, that would have been the end of our day. Instead it was a small, annoying thing. The box weighs three kilos, and I would carry it for ten hours again.

qa.q: Who is the team's repair person?
qa.a: Seema is the team's repair person.

qa.q: How did the team feel about the loose wire?
qa.a: They were annoyed but calm, since it was a small annoying thing and not the end of the day.

qa.q: What else could the team pack in the kit?
qa.a: They could add a printed wiring diagram and spare screws, since the more they can fix quickly, the fewer surprises ruin a run.

qa.q: How might Seema see the repair role?
qa.a: Seema probably feels important and focused, since fixing things is her only job, though it may also bring some pressure.

grounding: The team packs spare batteries, sensors, wires and tools and assigns one member to repair, so a broken part is an inconvenience rather than the end of the run.

subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
subtype: Approach: contingency plan with spare parts [Thinking]
passage: I drove Damini and Urmila to the robotics event in Pune, so I heard the whole plan from the back seat. Damini had a list. "Spare batteries, two. Spare IR sensors, three. Jumper wires, zip ties, the small screwdriver set, the glue gun." Urmila asked why so much. Damini said, "Because if one sensor dies at nine, we don't want our day to die at nine." She had also decided Urmila would be the fixer: during runs, Urmila would do nothing but watch for problems, toolbox open. In the second round a wheel cable snapped. From the gallery I saw Urmila swap it in about four minutes while Damini explained the pause to the judges. I don't know if they were nervous inside. They looked like people who had already imagined this moment.

qa.q: How many spare IR sensors did Damini pack?
qa.a: Damini packed three spare IR sensors.

qa.q: Why did Damini pack so many spares?
qa.a: Damini was wary of one broken part ending their whole day, so she planned ahead to stay calm if something failed.

qa.q: What else could strengthen their backup plan?
qa.a: They could practise a few repairs at home and time them, so the fixer knows which swaps are quick and which need help.

qa.q: How might Urmila see the fixer role?
qa.a: Urmila, first surprised at all the spares, gets a clear job and swaps the cable in four minutes, which likely makes Urmila feel trusted and useful.

grounding: Shows a team packing spare batteries, sensors, wires and tools and naming one member as fixer, so a broken cable on the day is only a short delay.

subtopic: Preparing for a science or robotics competition
subtype: Approach: contingency plan with spare parts [Thinking]
passage:
Two weeks before. Amandeep spread the robot's parts on the floor and asked Disha, "What could break on the day?" They listed it: the battery, the ultrasonic sensor, the loose wheel, the USB cable. "Then we carry one of each," Amandeep said. "And one of us only fixes." Disha volunteered.
The night before. Disha packed the spare parts into a tiffin box, labelled each with masking tape, and practised swapping the battery, timing herself on her phone.
Competition day. Ten minutes before their final run, the battery read nearly empty. Amandeep's face went pale. Disha had the tiffin open before anyone spoke. One minute forty seconds later, the robot was running. They finished third. On the bus home, Amandeep held up the empty tiffin. "Best thing we built all year."

qa.q: Where did Disha pack the spare parts?
qa.a: Disha packed them in a tiffin box.

qa.q: What was Amandeep feeling when the battery read nearly empty?
qa.a: Amandeep felt a jolt of panic and went pale, until Disha's quick swap turned it into a small delay.

qa.q: What could the team add to the plan next year?
qa.a: They could keep a checklist of which spares were used and charge every battery the night before, so the same failure is less likely.

qa.q: How might Disha see the fixer role after the swap?
qa.a: Disha likely feels proud and useful, since the swap she practised at home saved their final run.

grounding: Illustrates a team listing what could break, packing spares and giving one member the repair job, so a flat battery on the day doesn't end the run.
